A chemist found herself in the 11 th Century, where she met the renowned physician Avicenna. In Avi-
cenna's laboratory, she discovered a blue elixir and a yellow mysterious stone. She brought them back
to 2026. Determined to uncover their composition, she began her research.

Part 1. The blue elixir
At first, the chemist compiled a table listing the names of the only four plants which she saw in Avicenna’s
lab that could have been used to prepare the elixir, and the compounds that can be extracted from these
plants.

2: a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane skeleton bearing OH and three methyl substituents
(one bridgehead gem-dimethyl plus one methyl; C10H18O); no wedge/dash bonds are
printed.
3: an oxygen-bridged bicyclo[2.2.2]octane ether bearing one methyl and one
gem-dimethyl carbon (C10H18O); no wedge/dash bonds are printed.
4: a six-carbon unbranched chain with one internal C=C bond and terminal CH2OH
(C6H12O).
5: a benzene bearing adjacent OH and OCH3 groups and, para to OH, a
CH2-CH=CH2 group (C10H12O2).
6: the open chain CH2=CH-C(OH)(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH=C(CH3)-CH3 (C10H18O).
7: an azulene graph (fused five- and seven-membered aromatic rings) bearing an
ethyl group and two methyl groups (C14H16).
8: the acyclic branched tetraene
CH2=CH-C(=CH2)-CH2-CH2-CH=C(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH=C(CH3)2 (C15H24); no ring is
present.
9: a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptan-2-one framework bearing three methyl substituents
(C10H16O); no wedge/dash bonds are printed.
10: a cyclopentanone graph fused to a cyclopropane and bearing methyl and
isopropyl substituents (printed formula C10H18O); no wedge/dash bonds are
printed.
Rows map Zingiber to 1,2,3; Hypericum to 4,5,6; Chamomilla to 7,8,3; and
Artemisia to 9,10,3.

Chromatography also revealed it was substance Z that gave the elixir its blue colour. Z is a derivative
of the well-known substance A, which has two perpendicular planes of symmetry. When heated, A iso-
merises into aromatic compound B, which has three mutually perpendicular planes of symmetry. When
substance Z is chlorinated, a pair of peaks with an intensity ratio of 3:1 is observed in the mass spectrum
at m/z 218 and 220, respectively.

    1.2     Identify Z and draw the structures of substances A and B.                            4.0 pt


The chemist extracted W from the elixir. When W was added to an aqueous Fe3+ solution, a charac-
teristic colour change was observed. Mass spectrometric analysis of W revealed the intensity ratio of
[M]+ ∶ [M + 1]+ = 9:1, where M is the molecular ion. Assume carbon consists exclusively of 12 C and 13 C,
the natural isotopic abundance of 12 C is 98.9%, and all other elements are monoisotopic.

    1.3     Determine the number of carbon atoms (𝑛) from the mass spec data and                 3.0 pt
            identify W. Show your calculations.



Part 2. The mysterious stone
Avicenna had told her the stone was a stoichiometric compound. She dissolved it in dilute nitric acid.
After that, she adjusted the pH of the solution to ~4 and added NaF. This led to the formation of pre-
cipitate C ⋅ 𝑥H2 O, which contained 39.16% water by mass. Anhydrous C reacts with an excess of NaF to
yield compound D, which contains 32.85% sodium and 12.85% of metal Q by mass, and is used in the
industrial production of Q.




    1.4     Identify metal Q and compounds C ⋅ 𝑥H2 O and D.                                      4.0 pt


Avicenna told her that he found the stone in a coal deposit. The stone contains the anion of a highly
symmetrical acid F. Reaction of F with P2 O5 gives binary compound G, which contains 49.98% of oxygen
by mass and has a three-fold symmetry axis. F can be prepared by oxidising compound E with potassium
permanganate in an acidic solution. E contains 11.18% of hydrogen by mass and has a six-fold symmetry
axis.




    1.5     Draw the structures of E, F, and G.                                                  7.0 pt


Then, she analysed the stone thermogravimetrically in open air. A 10.00 g sample began to lose mass

Chromatography also revealed it was substance Z that gave the elixir its blue colour. Z is a derivative
of the well-known substance A, which has two perpendicular planes of symmetry. When heated, A iso-
merises into aromatic compound B, which has three mutually perpendicular planes of symmetry. When
substance Z is chlorinated, a pair of peaks with an intensity ratio of 3:1 is observed in the mass spectrum
at m/z 218 and 220, respectively.

    1.2     Identify Z and draw the structures of substances A and B.                            4.0 pt


The chemist extracted W from the elixir. When W was added to an aqueous Fe3+ solution, a charac-
teristic colour change was observed. Mass spectrometric analysis of W revealed the intensity ratio of
[M]+ ∶ [M + 1]+ = 9:1, where M is the molecular ion. Assume carbon consists exclusively of 12 C and 13 C,
the natural isotopic abundance of 12 C is 98.9%, and all other elements are monoisotopic.

    1.3     Determine the number of carbon atoms (𝑛) from the mass spec data and                 3.0 pt
            identify W. Show your calculations.



Part 2. The mysterious stone
Avicenna had told her the stone was a stoichiometric compound. She dissolved it in dilute nitric acid.
After that, she adjusted the pH of the solution to ~4 and added NaF. This led to the formation of pre-
cipitate C ⋅ 𝑥H2 O, which contained 39.16% water by mass. Anhydrous C reacts with an excess of NaF to
yield compound D, which contains 32.85% sodium and 12.85% of metal Q by mass, and is used in the
industrial production of Q.




    1.4     Identify metal Q and compounds C ⋅ 𝑥H2 O and D.                                      4.0 pt


Avicenna told her that he found the stone in a coal deposit. The stone contains the anion of a highly
symmetrical acid F. Reaction of F with P2 O5 gives binary compound G, which contains 49.98% of oxygen
by mass and has a three-fold symmetry axis. F can be prepared by oxidising compound E with potassium
permanganate in an acidic solution. E contains 11.18% of hydrogen by mass and has a six-fold symmetry
axis.




    1.5     Draw the structures of E, F, and G.                                                  7.0 pt


Then, she analysed the stone thermogravimetrically in open air. A 10.00 g sample began to lose mass

Chromatography also revealed it was substance Z that gave the elixir its blue colour. Z is a derivative

merises into aromatic compound B, which has three mutually perpendicular planes of symmetry. When
substance Z is chlorinated, a pair of peaks with an intensity ratio of 3:1 is observed in the mass spectrum
at m/z 218 and 220, respectively.

    1.2     Identify Z and draw the structures of substances A and B.                            4.0 pt


The chemist extracted W from the elixir. When W was added to an aqueous Fe3+ solution, a charac-
teristic colour change was observed. Mass spectrometric analysis of W revealed the intensity ratio of
[M]+ ∶ [M + 1]+ = 9:1, where M is the molecular ion. Assume carbon consists exclusively of 12 C and 13 C,
the natural isotopic abundance of 12 C is 98.9%, and all other elements are monoisotopic.

    1.3     Determine the number of carbon atoms (𝑛) from the mass spec data and                 3.0 pt
            identify W. Show your calculations.



Part 2. The mysterious stone
Avicenna had told her the stone was a stoichiometric compound. She dissolved it in dilute nitric acid.
After that, she adjusted the pH of the solution to ~4 and added NaF. This led to the formation of pre-
cipitate C ⋅ 𝑥H2 O, which contained 39.16% water by mass. Anhydrous C reacts with an excess of NaF to
yield compound D, which contains 32.85% sodium and 12.85% of metal Q by mass, and is used in the
industrial production of Q.




    1.4     Identify metal Q and compounds C ⋅ 𝑥H2 O and D.                                      4.0 pt


Avicenna told her that he found the stone in a coal deposit. The stone contains the anion of a highly
symmetrical acid F. Reaction of F with P2 O5 gives binary compound G, which contains 49.98% of oxygen
by mass and has a three-fold symmetry axis. F can be prepared by oxidising compound E with potassium
permanganate in an acidic solution. E contains 11.18% of hydrogen by mass and has a six-fold symmetry
axis.




    1.5     Draw the structures of E, F, and G.                                                  7.0 pt

All molecular graphs in the monomer catalogue itself are black. In the
topology and reaction figures, black and red distinguish the two selected

A1 is a 1,3,5-triphenylbenzene with para-B(OH)2 on each outer phenyl
(3-connected); A2 is 1,4-benzenediboronic acid (2-connected); A3 is
tetra(4-boronophenyl)ethene (4-connected); A4 is tetra(4-boronophenyl)silane
(4-connected). B1 is a metal phthalocyanine-type square core with four
peripheral catechol pairs (4-connected); B2 is a naphthalene with two
catechol edges (four OH, 2-connected); B3 is hexahydroxytriphenylene (three
catechol edges, 3-connected). C1 is 4,4'-diaminobiphenyl (2-connected); C2
has a central diarylethene-like pair of benzene nodes and four para-
aminophenyl arms (4-connected); C3 is a metal tetrakis(4-aminophenyl)-
porphyrin (4-connected). D1 is hexakis(4-formylphenyl)benzene (6-connected);
D2 is 2,4,6-tris(4-formylphenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (3-connected); D3 is
tetrakis(4-formylphenyl)methane (4-connected); D4 is
2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-1,4-benzenedicarbaldehyde (2-connected). E1 is a
1,3,5-tris(cyanomethyl)benzene (three -CH2-CN arms, 3-connected).
The seven topology icons preserve colored building-block roles: tetragonal-1
is 4-connected black nodes joined by 2-connected red linkers; tetragonal-2
interchanges those color/connectivity roles; hexagonal-1 is 3-connected black
nodes plus 2-connected red linkers; hexagonal-2 alternates 3-connected black
and 3-connected red nodes; trigonal uses 6-connected black nodes and
2-connected red linkers; kagome uses 4-connected black nodes and 2-connected
red linkers; tetrahedral is the three-dimensional diamond net of 4-connected
black nodes and 2-connected red linkers.
COF-3 is made from benzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde plus 2,5-dihydroxybenzene-1,4-diamine, then oxidized to COF-4. COF-5 is made from 2,4,6-trihydroxybenzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde plus p-phenylenediamine, then oxidized to COF-6. In this problem you are asked to be creative and build molecules from fragments. For instance, if you

below.




Cardiolipins are a family of acyclic phospholipids differing in fatty acid residues. They are essential for
energy production and membrane stability. Defects can lead to certain diseases. PL1 belongs to this
family. Using only the structural elements a-d in the quantities stated below, it is possible to assemble
the non-ionised form of PL1. R is a hydrocarbon substituent in the fatty acid structure.




PL1 does not contain any peroxide bonds.

     5.1     Tick one correct statement regarding the value of n (number of type a frag-             1.0 pt
             ments).
             (a) n is an even number,
             (b) n is an odd number,

Some cardiolipins are chiral molecules, even if they contain four identical fatty acid residues, as in the case
of PL1. One enantiomer of PL1 is found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and the other only in archaea. All
other diastereomers of PL1 are achiral molecules, since they have a plane of symmetry. Do not consider
the chirality of phosphorus atoms as stereocentres.
PL1 is a diprotic acid with the same acidic groups. Its second deprotonation is less favourable
(𝑝𝐾𝑎2 ≫ 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 ) due to the special, stable structure of monoanion Y.

Cardiolipins are a family of acyclic phospholipids differing in fatty acid residues. They are essential for
energy production and membrane stability. Defects can lead to certain diseases. PL1 belongs to this
family. Using only the structural elements a-d in the quantities stated below, it is possible to assemble
the non-ionised form of PL1. R is a hydrocarbon substituent in the fatty acid structure.




PL1 does not contain any peroxide bonds.

     5.1     Tick one correct statement regarding the value of n (number of type a frag-             1.0 pt
             ments).
             (a) n is an even number,
             (b) n is an odd number,
             (c) n can be either an odd or an even number.

Some cardiolipins are chiral molecules, even if they contain four identical fatty acid residues, as in the case
of PL1. One enantiomer of PL1 is found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and the other only in archaea. All
other diastereomers of PL1 are achiral molecules, since they have a plane of symmetry. Do not consider
the chirality of phosphorus atoms as stereocentres.
PL1 is a diprotic acid with the same acidic groups. Its second deprotonation is less favourable
(𝑝𝐾𝑎2 ≫ 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 ) due to the special, stable structure of monoanion Y.

In this problem you are asked to be creative and build molecules from fragments. For instance, if you
are required to draw a chiral phospholipid such as W using fragments a-e, it can be assembled as shown
below.




Cardiolipins are a family of acyclic phospholipids differing in fatty acid residues. They are essential for
energy production and membrane stability. Defects can lead to certain diseases. PL1 belongs to this
family. Using only the structural elements a-d in the quantities stated below, it is possible to assemble
the non-ionised form of PL1. R is a hydrocarbon substituent in the fatty acid structure.




PL1 does not contain any peroxide bonds.

     5.1     Tick one correct statement regarding the value of n (number of type a frag-             1.0 pt
             ments).
             (a) n is an even number,
             (b) n is an odd number,
             (c) n can be either an odd or an even number.

Some cardiolipins are chiral molecules, even if they contain four identical fatty acid residues, as in the case
of PL1. One enantiomer of PL1 is found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes, and the other only in archaea. All
other diastereomers of PL1 are achiral molecules, since they have a plane of symmetry. Do not consider
the chirality of phosphorus atoms as stereocentres.
PL1 is a diprotic acid with the same acidic groups. Its second deprotonation is less favourable
(𝑝𝐾𝑎2 ≫ 𝑝𝐾𝑎1 ) due to the special, stable structure of monoanion Y.

Audit scope: official G0, question-booklet, and answer-booklet source pages listed above. This section contains no marking-booklet content.
The starting graph is three linearly fused six-membered rings (an anthracene framework) whose ten perimeter sites are chlorinated. The sequence is starting material -2Cl radical -> A; A -5Cl radical -> B; B -2Cl radical -> C; C -Cl radical -> C14; and A -3Cl radical -> D. AFM panels A-D are grayscale bond-resolved images: A shows three fused-ring lobes with remaining peripheral bright Cl spots; B a shorter bent fused-carbon pattern; C an annular two-ring-intensity image; D an elongated zigzag carbon skeleton; C14 is a single circular ring image. The answer sheet preprints A as an anthracene graph bearing eight perimeter Cl atoms and two radical dots, at the upper non-fused carbon of the right ring and the lower non-fused carbon of the central ring; boxes B-D are blank.

and retro-Bergman (1) reactions on a surface. AFM images taken during the synthesis of C14 are shown
below:

The N2/CO2/H2 stream flows left through CO2 scrubber Z; N2/H2 go down to N2+3H2<=>2NH3. M2 flows right to cooler CLR; NH3 exits right, while unreacted N2/H2 recycle left to the reactor. Red arrows establish these directions.

The plant flow is: xCH4+yH2O enters steam reformer CH4+H2O->CO+3H2; that stream (CH4,CO,H2) enters partial oxidation 2CH4+O2->2CO+4H2 together with 4N2+1O2, yielding M1 downward to water-gas shift CO+H2O->CO2+H2 with H2O feed. The N2/CO2/H2 stream flows left through CO2 scrubber Z; N2/H2 go down to N2+3H2<=>2NH3. M2 flows right to cooler CLR; NH3 exits right, while unreacted N2/H2 recycle left to the reactor. Red arrows establish these directions.
The answer page is blank working space with a final m(CH4) line.

                                                                               Q7-2
Theory



                                                                                          English (Official)

Consider a model of a real reaction system, which includes recirculation of reagents. An open system
operates in a cyclic mode. Each cycle consists of four steps:
  1. A stoichiometric N2 : H2 = 1 : 3 mixture with a total amount of n0 mol is fed into the reactor after

The CD template is a top-view annulus. Seven (beta-CD) or six (alpha-CD) primary substituent boxes lie around the inner rim in cyclic order; a single outer box labelled (OH)14 for beta-CD or (OBn)12 for alpha-CD denotes the repeated secondary substituents. Red position numbers increase clockwise where printed.
Starting beta-CD positions 1-7 are printed clockwise with CH2OH in every primary box and (OH)14 outside. NaH (30 equiv), BnCl (30 equiv), then DIBAL-H (2 equiv) gives L. The later displayed dimer has two beta-CD rims joined by an -O-(CH2)8-O- bridge between primary CH2 groups; on each ring five primary boxes are CH2OBn, one is CH2OH, and one bridge-bearing box is CH2O-(CH2)8-OCH2; all fourteen secondary sites are OBn. The requested L answer template has seven blank primary boxes and one outside secondary-substituent box.
